name: GoodMeet – Google Meet Integration for Webinar, Meeting & Video Conference
author: Sovlix

sections.description:
📘 Documentation | 🔥 Get GoodMeet PRO | 🤝 Join Community | 🕹️ YouTube

GoodMeet lets you create, schedule and manage Google Meet meetings right from your WordPress site. It is built for educators, coaches, consultants, course creators and anyone who runs online classes, webinars or client calls.

Every meeting gets a Google Meet link, a Google Calendar event and its own page on your site. Pick a design for that page, embed meetings anywhere with shortcodes and blocks, and connect GoodMeet to your LMS, Google Classroom or WooCommerce store.

Features marked (Pro) need GoodMeet Pro. Everything else is in this free plugin.

New to GoodMeet? The step-by-step guides walk you through every feature, from connecting your Google account to selling meetings.

💡 Use Cases

  • Run live classes for your Tutor LMS, LearnPress, Academy LMS or LifterLMS courses.
  • Post meetings to your Google Classroom classes.
  • Sell consultations, webinars and online classes through WooCommerce.
  • Let marketplace vendors sell their own meetings on Dokan, WCFM or MultiVendorX.
  • Let instructors create and host meetings from the front end of your site.

🚀 Getting Started

  • Guided setup: a Get Started page walks you through connecting Google and creating your first meeting.
  • Your own Google Cloud project: upload your OAuth client file once, approve access, and one connection covers Google Meet, Google Calendar and Google Classroom.
  • Meeting wizard: create and edit meetings in clear steps: details, date and time, access and controls, page design.
  • Rich descriptions: write meeting descriptions in the WordPress editor, with headings, lists and links.
  • Meeting defaults: set the time zone, reminder and calendar rules once, and every new meeting starts with them.
  • Full guide: How to Connect Google Meet to WordPress

🎨 Meeting Page Themes

Every meeting has its own page on your site. Choose how it looks.

  • 2 free themes: Classic and Paper.
  • 12 Pro themes (Pro): Cover, Studio, Cadence, Guestlist, Admit, Lobby, Lesson, Keynote, Consult, Aurora, Journal and Encore, each made for a kind of meeting such as webinars, recurring standups, consultations or lessons.
  • Theme per meeting: set a site-wide theme, then pick a different one on any single meeting.
  • Style controls: brand colour, button shape, sidebar side, thumbnail, and hiding the theme header and footer.
  • Page background and custom background colour (Pro).
  • Clear meeting states: countdown before the start, a Join button while live, and an ended state once the meeting is over.

📅 Meetings & Google Calendar

  • Create Google Meet meetings with a Google Calendar event for each one.
  • Set the time zone, duration, reminder and event status.
  • Choose who gets calendar emails, whether the event shows as busy or free, and its visibility.
  • Countdown timer, add-to-calendar buttons and meeting thumbnails.
  • Duplicate meetings with one click.
  • Recurring meetings (Pro): daily, weekly, monthly or yearly, ending on a date, after a number of sessions, or never.
  • Registration (Pro): ask visitors for their name and email before they get the join link.
  • Page access (Pro): open to everyone, logged-in users only, or selected roles.
  • Password and co-hosts (Pro): protect a meeting and add co-hosts.

🧩 Shortcodes & Blocks

  • Meeting list shortcode: a searchable, sortable table of the meetings each visitor may open.
  • Single meeting shortcode with options to hide the details, timer or calendar box.
  • Google Meet block for the block editor and an Elementor widget.
  • Embedded meetings follow the same page access rule as the meeting page.

🎓 LMS Integration

Add Google Meet live classes to your courses.

  • Works with Tutor LMS, LearnPress, Academy LMS and LifterLMS (Pro).
  • Live classes on lessons and courses (Pro): instructors schedule a live class from the course editor, and enrolled students see it on the lesson with a countdown and Join button.
  • Course access (Pro): only enrolled students can join.
  • Each LMS has its own switch under Integrations.

🏫 Google Classroom

  • Turn on Google Classroom, see the classes you teach and their students, and post a meeting to a class stream. The post updates when you edit the meeting.
  • Create classes and send invites (Pro).
  • Link classes to Tutor LMS, LearnPress and Academy LMS courses (Pro).
  • Attendance, student sign-in and teacher and student dashboards (Pro).

👩‍🏫 Instructors & Front End

  • Instructors (Pro): add instructors who create and host their own meetings.
  • Front-end meetings (Pro): instructors create meetings from a dashboard page on your site, without wp-admin.
  • Instructor and student dashboards (Pro) with meetings, classes, students and attendance.
  • Students never see Google setup messages. Only admins and instructors do.

🛒 WooCommerce

  • Sell meetings (Pro): link a meeting to a WooCommerce product and sell tickets.
  • Buyers get the meeting details in their order email and in My Account.
  • Use any WooCommerce payment gateway.
  • WooCommerce Bookings (Pro): create a Google Meet meeting for each confirmed booking.

🏪 Multi-Vendor Marketplaces

  • Dokan, WCFM Marketplace and MultiVendorX (Pro): vendors sell their own meetings from their vendor dashboard.
  • Vendors use their own calendar: turn it on to let each vendor connect their own Google account from a Configure page. Turn it off and meetings use the site owner’s account.
  • Each marketplace has its own switch under Integrations.

✅ More

  • Works on phones and tablets, and the admin meets WCAG 2.2 AA.
  • Translation ready.
  • Built with React. The uncompiled source ships with the plugin.

  • TogMeet – Microsoft Teams Integration for Webinar, Meeting & Video Conference

External Services

This plugin connects to the Google Meet and Google Calendar APIs in order to create, manage, and synchronize meetings from your WordPress site.

What the service is and what it is used for:

  • Google Meet API is used to create and manage video meetings.
  • Google Calendar API is used to sync meeting times, send reminders, and manage calendar events.

What data is sent and when:

  • When creating or updating a meeting, the following data is sent to Google APIs:
    • Meeting title, description, date/time, timezone
    • Attendees’ email addresses (only if you add them)
    • Your connected Google account info (OAuth tokens, securely stored)
  • No data is sent unless you explicitly create a meeting or connect your Google account.

Google Classroom API (classroom.googleapis.com): used only if you turn on Google Classroom under GoodMeet > Classroom.

  • It reads the classes you teach and their student lists (names and email addresses), to show them in wp-admin. Student data is cached for 15 minutes and is not stored as WordPress users.
  • When you pick a class on a meeting, it posts an announcement to that class with the meeting title, time, description and a link to the meeting page, updates it when you edit the meeting, and deletes it when you delete the meeting.
  • Nothing is sent to Google Classroom while this option is off.
  • Covered by the same Google Terms of Service and Google Privacy Policy listed below.

Freemius is used for plugin licensing (activating GoodMeet Pro), and for basic usage telemetry that helps us maintain compatibility and provide support.
It automatically sends non-sensitive site data (site URL, PHP/WordPress version, plugin version, and license/premium status) on admin pages while the plugin is active. Admin email is only sent if you opt in during the connection/activation screen.
This service is provided by Freemius, Inc.: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

Terms of Service and Privacy Policy:

  • Google Terms of Service
  • Google Privacy Policy

To use these features, users must authenticate with their Google account via OAuth. All API interactions follow Google’s security and privacy guidelines.

Source Code

The admin interface is built with React and compiled to the minified JavaScript shipped in assets/dist/. The uncompiled source is in assets/src/, with package.json and composer.json in the plugin root.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins > Add New Plugin and search for GoodMeet.
  2. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  3. Go to GoodMeet > Get Started and follow the steps to connect your Google account.
  4. Create your first meeting under GoodMeet > All Meetings > Add New.

Step-by-step guides with screenshots: sovlix.com/docs.
sections.faq:
Where can I find the documentation?

All guides are at sovlix.com/docs. They cover setup, meetings, themes, LMS, Google Classroom, WooCommerce and marketplaces, step by step with screenshots.

Does this plugin support platforms other than Google Meet?

No. GoodMeet is built only for Google Meet. For Zoom, Jitsi, Webex and Microsoft Teams, see our other plugins listed above.

Do I need a paid Google Cloud plan?

No. You create a free Google Cloud project, enable the Google Meet and Google Calendar APIs, and upload its OAuth client file to GoodMeet. No billing account is needed.

Do I need Google Calendar connected?

Yes. GoodMeet creates each meeting’s Meet link through a Google Calendar event, so the Calendar API is part of the one Google connection.

Can I change how the meeting page looks?

Yes. Pick a theme under GoodMeet > Settings > Meeting themes, and change it on any single meeting. Classic and Paper are free; 12 more themes come with GoodMeet Pro.

Can I restrict meeting access?

Yes, with GoodMeet Pro. A meeting can be open to everyone, logged-in users or selected roles, need registration, or have a password. LMS live classes are limited to enrolled students.

Will this work with my LMS?

Yes, with GoodMeet Pro. It works with Tutor LMS, LearnPress, Academy LMS and LifterLMS: live classes on lessons and courses, limited to enrolled students.

Do I need GoodMeet Pro for Google Classroom?

No. The free plugin turns Classroom on, lists your classes and students, and posts meetings to a class stream. Creating classes, invites, course links, attendance and dashboards need GoodMeet Pro.

Can vendors use their own Google account?

Yes. Turn on Vendors use their own calendar under GoodMeet > Settings > Meetings. Each vendor then connects their own account from a Configure page in their vendor dashboard.
sections.changelog:
2.1.0 – 3 Oct, 2026

  • New: Meeting page themes, with a Meeting themes screen under Settings and a preview of each theme.
  • New: Pick a theme for a single meeting, or leave it on the site default.
  • New: Style settings for meeting pages: brand colour, button shape, sidebar side, thumbnail, and hiding the site header and footer.
  • New: Meeting descriptions use the WordPress editor on the admin and front-end meeting forms, so headings, lists and links are kept.
  • New: The Google Classroom screen lists courses from Tutor LMS, LearnPress and Academy LMS.
  • New: A meeting page now shows an ended state once the meeting time has passed.
  • New: Documentation link to the step-by-step guides at https://sovlix.com/docs/.
  • Security: The meeting list no longer exposes meeting passwords to visitors.
  • Security: An embedded meeting now follows the same page access rule as its meeting page.
  • Fix: The sidebar Left and Right settings were swapped on some meeting pages.
  • Fix: Duration presets, the recurring end date, switching Google accounts, and the error shown when the wrong file is uploaded.
  • Fix: Settings headings ran into their descriptions on the WCFM vendor dashboard.
  • Improvement: The Required badge on the Google Cloud Credentials card is hidden once the account is connected.
  • Compatibility: Meetings and settings saved before this release keep working with the new themes.

2.0.0 – 29 Sep, 2026

  • New: Fully redesigned admin: All Meetings, Settings, Integrations and a new Get Started page.
  • New: Step-by-step meeting wizard for creating and editing meetings.
  • New: Frontend Meetings screen replaces Add-ons, with a guided setup for the members page.
  • New: Dokan, WCFM and MultiVendorX each have their own switch under Integrations.
  • New: Live now banner on All Meetings while a meeting is running.
  • Improvement: Every screen works on phones and tablets, and meets WCAG 2.2 AA.
  • Fix: Google connection no longer drops after one hour.
  • Fix: Meeting shortcode showed PHP warnings and the wrong topic.
  • Fix: Meeting list shortcode showed nothing when there were no meetings.
  • Fix: Vendors can connect their own Google account from every supported marketplace.

1.2.5 – 19 Aug, 2026

  • Security: Update security.

1.2.4 – 18 Aug, 2026

  • Security: Update security.

1.2.3 – 12 Aug, 2026

  • Updated Freemius SDK to 2.13.4.

1.2.2 – 12 Aug, 2026

  • Enhanced performance and security.

1.2.1 – 24 Jun, 2026

  • Security: Enhanced security improvements.

1.2.0 – 22 Jun, 2026

  • New: Added vendor Google Calendar configuration pages for multivendor platforms (Dokan, MultiVendorX, and WCFM)
  • New: Vendors can now connect and manage their own Google Calendar accounts directly from their vendor dashboard
  • New: Added a dedicated Configure section under Google Meeting for vendor-specific Google Calendar authentication and settings
  • New: Introduced vendor-level Google Meeting settings, allowing each vendor to manage their own calendar integration independently
  • New: When “Allow Vendors to Connect Their Own Google Calendar” is enabled, meetings created by vendors can now be synced to their connected Google Calendar account instead of the store administrator’s calendar
  • Enhancement: Improved multivendor workflow to better support individual vendor scheduling and prevent shared-calendar conflicts
  • Fix: Resolved an issue where vendor dashboards did not provide a Google Calendar connection interface, causing meetings to be created using the administrator’s Google Calendar account. This affected Dokan, MultiVendorX, and WCFM multivendor integrations.

1.1.12 – 16 Jun, 2026

  • Enhancement: Updated Freemius SDK to the latest version

1.1.11 – 16 Jun, 2026

  • Fix: Google Meet meeting summary can now be cleared from WordPress; previously clearing the field had no effect on Google’s side
  • Compatibility: Tested up to WordPress 7.0

1.1.9 – 08 May 2026

  • Security fix: Enhanced security improvements.

1.1.8 – 07 May 2026

  • Security fix: Enhanced security improvements.

1.1.6 – 26 December 2025

  • Updated Freemius SDK

  • Minor bug fixes and improvements.

  • Updated Freemius SDK

1.1.3 – 12 July 2025

  • Resolved various bugs and stability issues
  • Refreshed and updated the tutorial link for better guidance

1.1.2 – 03 July 2025

1.1.0 – 21 June 2025

  • Introduced numerous new features.
